newsitem.title: USA: Tribune Q3 operating profit increases.
newsitem.headline: Tribune Q3 operating profit increases.

text.p: Tribune Co said Friday overall operating profit rose 40 percent in the third quarter.
It said broadcasting and entertainment operating profit was up 18 percent to $41 million from $35 million a year ago due primarily to improvements at the Chicago Cubs and in the radio group.

Publishing operating profit climbed 17 percent to $61 million due to gains from all newspapers. Tribune's education group posted quarterly operating profit of $22 million compared to $3 million in 1995 due to contributions from recent acquisitions.

Tribune reported third quarter earnings of $0.92 per diluted share, up from $0.73 a year ago. The 1995 results included a gain of $0.18 per share from discontinued operations and a loss of $0.07 per share on the sale of Times Advocate Co.
Revenues advanced to $618.3 million from $552.2 million.
Chairman John Madigan in a statement said the company has "a strong competitive advantage for further growth in broadcasting."

In publishing, advertising revenues rose six percent. Tribune said newsprint and ink expense decreased 14 percent, as average newsprint prices fell 10 percent. Consumption declined five percent due to linage and copy decreases.
Other expenses were up nine percent, mainly due to increased development of Internet and online-related businesses.
"Newspapers are the front door to the Internet, and we lead the field with our ongoing development of compelling online content," Madigan added.
